content:
anya: Heads-up: we need a decision on how to merge partial traces from the inference-sidecar + runtime for accurate token billing. Seen customers double-billed in last invoice sample.

lucy: Can you sketch the root cause? Sidecar and runtime both emitting token-related metrics?

anya: Exactly. Sidecar emits 'prefix_cache' spans with tokens_estimate, runtime emits per-token spans with tokens_emitted. In analytics they end up as separate traces and both contribute to billed tokens.

sam: Reconciliation options: 1) ingest-time stitch/join by request id, 2) query-time dedupe using heuristics, 3) change producer contracts so only runtime reports token counts and sidecar emits metadata-only.

kevin: We discussed producer contract before. Changing producers is safest long-term but slow. For short term we need an ingest-time mitigation.

anya: I prefer a hybrid: producer contract + short ingest window stitch. If runtime span arrives within W seconds, prefer it for numeric metrics; otherwise fall back to heuristics.

lucy: What about multi-model fanout? One request may fan out to model A and B; tokens should be billed to the model that generated them. How do we avoid collapsing distinct model traces?

sam: Stitch key must include model_id and request_id, not just request_id. Proposed stitch_key = [tenant_id, request_id, model_id, region_shard]. Model_id keeps fanout separate.

kevin: region_shard helps with request_id collisions across regions. We should also push for UUIDv7 request IDs to make collisions practically impossible.

anya: Reconciliation policy (draft):

```text
- stitch_key = [tenant_id, request_id, model_id, region_shard]
- authoritative_source_priority = [runtime, inference-sidecar, proxy]
- reconciliation_window = 30s (configurable)
- numeric_merge = prefer_authoritative_for(tokens_emitted, tokens_estimate)
- sidecar spans with role=helper -> keep only metadata except when runtime missing after window
```

lucy: Nice. Two operational questions: memory footprint for a keyed-window join; and sampling alignment since sampling at source could drop one side of the pair.

kevin: For memory, a stateful operator (rocks-backed) helps but increases tail latencies. We should benchmark: approximate expected unique keys per second for cost-accounting subset. If >X, fallback to query-time dedupe for that tenant cohort.

sam: Sampling: enforce deterministic sampling by request_id for any traces used in billing. If request_id hash % N -> sample decision, propagate sampling header so both sidecar and runtime keep the same decision. Add this to the instrumentation checklist.

anya: We'll need small schema additions: optional string span.role, optional string model_id, optional string region_shard, optional number tokens_emitted, optional number tokens_estimate. Defaults null for older agents. Add docs to explain semantics.

kevin: Also consider migrating token accounting to a compact billing topic instead of full trace storage. Ingest dedupe writes a single billing event per stitch_key; raw spans still land in cold storage. That minimizes long-term storage duplication.

lucy: Tradeoffs: ingest dedupe reduces storage and simplifies billing queries but costs CPU/memory during ingest. Query-time dedupe leaves raw data intact and is easier to roll back. We should codify both in RFC and propose a canary path.

anya: Rollout plan idea:
- Phase 0: producer contract + sampling header spec (docs and SDK updates)
- Phase 1: ingest stitch for 5% of traffic (billing topic only), monitor duplicate-cost-rate, memory usage, and billing deltas
- Phase 2: ramp to 25% then 100% if metrics look good; keep raw traces in cold bucket for 7d
- Phase 3: update console docs + customer comms about attribution change

sam: Metrics to watch: duplicate-cost-rate (>0.5% alert), billing-delta-percent, ingest-operator-memory, stitch-latency, missed-runtime-count (cases where runtime never arrives).

kevin: If runtime never arrives, we should honor sidecar's tokens_estimate but tag the billing event with fallback_reason=missing_runtime so we can audit.

obs-bot: Note: I will create alert: obs.duplicate_cost_rate > 0.5% sustained 1h. Temp suppression requested during canary?

anya: Request suppression for the canary window but keep high-severity paging if >5%. Also create a dashboard for before/after per-tenant comparisons.

lucy: Owners: eng-platform (anya, lucy) to draft RFC + console blurb; eng-runtime (kevin) to run ingest-state benchmark; infra (sam) to add sampling header enforcement and canary flag.

anya: I'll open the RFC PR and include sample merge config and rollout checklist. Meeting to review RFC next Tue 09:30 PT.

kevin: One last thought: include a small open-source example (node/python) showing how to set sampling header and span.role to help integrations teams.

anya: Good call. Add to RFC checklist. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
